questions.questionText: Xylem vessel elements are specialised cells that are adapted for the transport of water. Which statement correctly matches an adaptation of a xylem vessel element to its function?

options.A: Cytoplasm is only found in a thin layer next to the cell walls and does not contain any organelles. This reduces resistance to the flow of water in the xylem vessels.
options.B: The end walls between xylem vessel elements have partially broken down, forming end plates. This reduces resistance to the flow of water in the xylem vessel.
options.C: The walls of the xylem vessel elements contain cellulose that is hydrophilic and can form hydrogen bonds to water, allowing adhesion of water molecules to the vessel walls.
options.D: Xylem vessel elements have plasmodesmata that connect them with companion cells. The companion cells provide ATP, which is needed for the transport of water.

questions.questionText: A student makes an accurate labelled plan diagram of a section of a leaf containing a vascular bundle. Which statement correctly describes part of their plan diagram?

options.A: The vascular bundle has labels for the xylem vessel elements, phloem sieve tube elements and companion cells.
options.B: The vascular bundle is divided into two sections, with the section closer to the upper epidermis labelled as xylem and the other section labelled as phloem.
options.C: In the section of the vascular bundle positioned closer to the lower epidermis, each sieve tube element has an associated companion cell.
options.D: The phloem sieve tube elements are drawn with thick cell walls to represent the lignin in the walls.

questions.questionText: Some babies are born with a hole between the right and left atria. These babies are found to have an increased number of red blood cells. What is the reason for this increase in red blood cells in these babies?

options.A: Blood is pumped faster, which causes more blood to circulate in the heart.
options.B: More blood is needed in the heart because the pressure is lower.
options.C: Their haemoglobin has a higher affinity for oxygen.
options.D: There is a lower oxygen concentration in the body of the newborn baby.

questions.questionText: An increase in carbon dioxide in human blood shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the right. What is the explanation for this effect?

options.B: Carbon dioxide is more soluble than oxygen and displaces it.
options.C: Diffusion of carbon dioxide between the alveoli and the blood is more rapid.
options.D: Increasing the H+ concentration decreases haemoglobin affinity for oxygen.
